channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Astana to Restrict Traffic and Conduct Military Aviation Flights November 5-7
item.description: Astana will temporarily restrict traffic on certain streets from November 5 to 7, 2026, due to preparations for international political events. Special state and law enforcement agencies, along with the Armed Forces of Kazakhstan, will ensure security. Military aviation training flights will also take place in the capital's airspace starting November 1.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo: Death Toll Surpasses 5,000
item.description: The Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed over 5,000 lives, with confirmed cases exceeding 10,000. Approximately half of those infected have died, making it the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. The spread is attributed to the Bundibugyo virus, for which no approved vaccine currently exists.

item.title: Russian Billionaires Lose Over $28 Billion Year-to-Date
item.description: Russian billionaires have collectively lost over $28 billion since the beginning of the year. The president of Norilsk Nickel experienced the largest financial decline, with his wealth decreasing by $8.1 billion to $21.6 billion. Alexey Mordashov saw the smallest loss, with his fortune reduced by $515 million to $27.8 billion.

item.title: Kazakhstan and OPEC+ Agree to Maintain December Oil Production Quotas
item.description: Key OPEC+ participants, including Kazakhstan, have tentatively agreed to keep December oil production targets unchanged during an online meeting on November 1. This decision aligns with expectations, with further policy adjustments deferred to next year. The group, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, is navigating the recovery of oil exports amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Iran Designates British Navy and Air Force as Terrorist Organizations
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry announced "retaliatory measures" against the UK on November 1, 2026. British foreign intelligence (MI6) is now considered a "hostile group," while the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force have been designated as terrorist organizations. These actions are Iran's response to what it calls "hostile actions" by London over the past year.

item.title: Reservoir Explosion at Rogun Hydropower Plant Under Construction in Tajikistan
item.description: An explosion occurred at a reservoir at the Rogun Hydropower Plant under construction in Tajikistan. Authorities claim no one was injured, while independent media report casualties. The State Supervision Service attributed the incident to a rupture in a technical water collection reservoir, causing water to flood a tunnel. Radio Ozodi, citing sources, reports over five workers were injured.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened Against Imarat Development Management in Tashkent After Buyer Complaints
item.description: Tashkent's Internal Affairs Directorate has opened a criminal case against the construction company Imarat Development following complaints from citizens who expressed distrust in its operations. Buyers demanded refunds for properties located outside Tashkent, but the company allegedly failed to return the funds. Cases were initiated under fraud and abuse of power articles.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Processed Agricultural Exports Exceed 54% of Total
item.description: Kazakhstan's exports of high-value-added agro-industrial products are steadily increasing. For the first eight months of 2026, processed agricultural exports reached $3.04 billion, a 35.1% increase year-on-year. Processed goods now account for over 54.1% of total agricultural exports, indicating improved competitiveness of Kazakh products abroad.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 400 People Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 108 families, totaling 464 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that returnees entered through Torkham, Spin Boldak, Silk Bridge, and Islam Qala crossings. The majority, 259 people from 67 families, returned via the Silk Bridge in Nimroz province.

item.title: Free Nations League Movements Urge Against Russia's Observer Status in OTS
item.description: Movements within the Free Nations League have called for Russia not to be granted observer status in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS). The appeal highlights concerns regarding Russia's role and potential influence within the regional organization.

item.title: UN-Habitat: Aid Insufficient for Repairing Shelters of Returnee Families in Herat
item.description: UN-Habitat is assisting vulnerable returnee families in Herat with shelter repairs, supported by the UN Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan. The project aims to provide security and dignity. However, UN-Habitat stated that current aid is insufficient and more support is needed, emphasizing adequate housing as a human right.

item.title: Poland's Constitutional Dispute Intensifies as PM Refuses Compromise with President
item.description: Poland's constitutional dispute around the Constitutional Tribunal has escalated. President Andrzej Duda returned to Warsaw, meeting with the tribunal's dismissed president. Prime Minister Donald Tusk sharply criticized the president's actions, stating he would not compromise to restore the rule of law.

item.title: New Polio Vaccination Campaign to Launch Across Afghanistan Tomorrow
item.description: A new polio vaccination campaign is set to begin nationwide tomorrow, Monday, November 2nd. The 'Afghanistan Free of Polio' page urged citizens to participate in eradicating polio. Afghanistan and Pakistan remain the only countries where polio has not been eradicated.

item.title: Two Men Arrested in Kostanay for Extorting 17 Million Tenge and Threats
item.description: Two previously convicted men have been arrested in Kostanay for extorting 17 million tenge and threatening violence. They were apprehended on October 28 while receiving 4.4 million tenge. The suspects are being held in a temporary detention center as the investigation continues.

item.title: Polish PM Tusk Accuses Russia of Supporting Opposition in Political Crisis
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused Russia of supporting his opponents amid a political crisis, stating that Russian bots are backing them online. Tusk criticized the ruling Law and Justice party and President Andrzej Duda for undermining the rule of law. He also accused President Duda of refusing to swear in new Constitutional Tribunal judges.

item.title: Lisbon Police Clear New Protest Camp Against High Housing Costs
item.description: Lisbon police dismantled a protest camp on Rossio Square on November 1, established by activists demonstrating against the government's housing policy. The protesters are demanding the government abandon a bill that would change rental and eviction rules. Police used shields and batons to clear the camp.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Phased Rollout of Electronic Entry Permit System
item.description: Starting November 1, Kazakhstan is gradually implementing an electronic entry permit system, QazETA, for citizens of visa-free countries and EAEU nations. Initially available at Aktau airport and specific land border crossings, it will become mandatory by July 1, 2027. The permit is valid for 180 days and is free of charge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Companies Sign Agreements Worth $95 Million
item.description: Companies from Kazakhstan have signed agreements and contracts totaling $95 million following a trade and economic mission in Bishkek. The mission, part of the Second Forum of Interregional Cooperation, involved around 80 Kazakh companies exploring export expansion, joint investment projects, and direct business ties with Kyrgyz partners.

item.title: UNAMA chief visits Nangarhar province in Afghanistan
item.description: The head of the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA), Rabab Fatima, has made her first provincial visit to Nangarhar. During her trip, she met with local authorities, women, elders, businesspeople, returnees, and UN agencies. The visit aims to understand the needs and key issues in the province. UNAMA reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Afghanistan.

item.title: Criminal case opened against Imarat Development LLC management in Tashkent
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against the management of Imarat Development LLC in Tashkent. The company, with offices in Sergeli district, allegedly failed to inform buyers that homes were being built in the Tashkent region and did not return funds. The Internal Affairs Directorate has opened a case for fraud and abuse of authority.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Corn Fields Exceed Astana's Area Amid Agricultural Expansion
item.description: Corn plantings in Kazakhstan have surged by 60% to 106,000 hectares, surpassing the area of Astana. This expansion is driven by new processing plants, including 'Kazkrakhmal' in Turkestan region, and several other large-scale projects aimed at producing starches, gluten, and bioethanol for export.

item.title: Kazakhstan Activist Launches Petition to Ban Religious Education for Minors
item.description: A Kazakhstani activist, Asel Tauhan, has launched a petition proposing a ban on religious education for children under 18. She argues that some religious materials may pose hidden threats to minors' safety and rights, including justifying early marriages and infringing on women's rights. The petition, titled 'Religion Can Wait Until 18,' aims to address concerns about the content of religious instruction.

item.title: FBI Accuses North Korea of Stealing Over $6 Billion from Binance
item.description: The FBI has accused North Korea of being behind a cyberattack on the Binance crypto exchange, resulting in the theft of over $6 billion. The exchange has pledged to cover financial losses and announced a phased resumption of withdrawals. The FBI linked the attack to North Korean cyber activity known as TraderTraitor.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Entry and Stay Regulations for Foreign Citizens
item.description: New regulations for the entry and stay of foreigners in Kazakhstan will be implemented starting November 1st at one airport and four vehicle checkpoints. Citizens from 85 countries will need an electronic permit via the QazETA system. The phased rollout begins November 1, 2026, at Aktau Airport and specific checkpoints, with international airports in Astana and Almaty to follow in 2027.

item.title: Two Men Arrested in Kostanay for Extorting 17 Million Tenge
item.description: Two men were apprehended in Kostanay while extorting 17 million tenge from a victim. According to investigators, they threatened the victim with violence to demand the money. Previously convicted individuals were caught receiving 4.4 million tenge.

item.title: Man Arrested for 15 Days in Almaty for Inciting Trucker Protest
item.description: A man in Almaty has been sentenced to 15 days in jail for calling on truck drivers to protest restrictions on truck axle loads. He urged drivers to stop working on November 1, arguing that heavy trucks are essential for the city's construction infrastructure.

item.title: Turkish Daesh Suspect Uğur Bahadır Arrested in Pakistan, Trained in Balochistan
item.description: Turkish national Uğur Bahadır, a suspected Daesh member, reportedly arrived in Islamabad and received training at a Daesh camp in Balochistan, Pakistan. Sources claim he was arrested in Pakistan in March 2025, contradicting Turkish media reports of a recent capture in the Afghanistan-Pakistan region.

item.title: 15 Years Since Taraz Terror Attack: How One Man Claimed Multiple Lives in Two Hours
item.description: Fifteen years ago, on November 12, 2011, a devastating terror attack struck Taraz, Kazakhstan. Armed assailant Maksat Kariev carried out multiple attacks, including a gun store robbery and shootings targeting police officers, resulting in seven deaths and injuries. Police Captain Gaziz Baitasov died protecting civilians.

item.title: Trump Reiterates Iran Seeks Deal, Claims Talks Progressing Well
item.description: President Trump stated Iran desires a deal and that negotiations are progressing well, though he expressed skepticism about their reliability. He reiterated claims about damaging Iran's military capabilities and threatened strikes on a nuclear facility.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agricultural Product Exports Increased by 35 Percent
item.description: Kazakhstan is prioritizing the development of its deep processing sector for grain and increasing finished product exports. This year, exports of processed agricultural products grew by 35 percent. Six major investment projects totaling $4 billion are planned.

item.title: Nigeria Investigating Two Suspected Ebola Cases in Northeast Region
item.description: Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control is investigating two suspected Ebola cases in the country's northeast. The individuals are quarantined, and contact tracing is underway. Confirmation awaits laboratory test results, following the country's first Ebola case in over a decade last week.

item.title: Ukraine Forces Strike Russian Rocket Fuel Plant in Rostov Region
item.description: Ukraine's armed forces claim to have struck a plant in Russia's Rostov region producing solid fuel for missiles. The General Staff reported that attack drones and Neptune missiles were used, causing a fire and damaging production workshops. This action aims to reduce Russia's ability to shell Ukrainian settlements.

item.title: Protests in Germany escalate to riots, with Molotov cocktails and vandalism
item.description: Youth protests organized by the 'Gen-Z regelt' movement in major German cities have turned violent. In Frankfurt, protesters smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Berlin reported 56 arrests, while Cologne banned a march. Over 100,000 participated nationwide.

item.title: FBI blames North Korean group TraderTraitor for Binance hack and $6 billion theft
item.description: The FBI has accused the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor of stealing over $6 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. The group is reportedly converting stolen assets into Ethereum and laundering them through DeFi services. The FBI has published wallet addresses and urged sector participants to block transactions.

item.title: Polish Prime Minister Accuses President Amid Constitutional Tribunal Crisis
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk addressed the nation, accusing the opposition party 'Law and Justice' and President Andrzej Duda of violence against Constitutional Tribunal members and undermining the rule of law. Tusk refused compromise, stating the tribunal must operate independently and constitutionally.

item.title: Iran's Army Spokesperson Confirms Purchase of Russian Su-35 Fighter Jets
item.description: Iran's army spokesperson, Mohammad Akrami-Nia, announced the purchase of Russian Su-35 fighter jets, stating they are expected after the war concludes. He mentioned that preparations and training were completed before the conflict with the US and Israel began, and delivery is imminent.

item.title: US Open to Playing Role in Pakistan-Afghanistan Security Concerns, Says Senator Rubio
item.description: Senator Marco Rubio indicated US willingness to play a constructive role in addressing Pakistan's security concerns regarding alleged attacks from Afghan territory. Washington opposes terrorism regardless of its origin or target.

item.title: US Secretary of State Reaffirms Commitment to Defense Agreement With Saudi Arabia
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the United States will continue to uphold its defense cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia. This commitment remains in place despite ongoing hostilities involving Yemen’s Houthis. Rubio made these remarks at a news conference on the sidelines of the G20 summit.

item.title: Trump Claims Iran Seeks Deal, Negotiations Progressing Well
item.description: Former U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran is seeking a deal and that negotiations are proceeding favorably. This comment comes amid ongoing discussions regarding Iran's nuclear program and international relations.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Foreign Trade Deficit Reaches $13.7 Billion in Nine Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade deficit reached $13.7 billion in the first nine months of the year. Exports decreased due to a sharp decline in gold sales, while imports significantly increased. The total foreign trade turnover amounted to $65.4 billion during the period.
